correctness.rationale: For four independent surface-uniform points on S², Euclidean unsigned tetrahedral volume is D|n·P4−h|/6, D the triangle cross-product length from the first triple. Projected-sphere inverse-distance potential equals π/2 for every line meeting the unit ball; conditioning on the first two points yields E(D⁻¹|P1,P2)=π/(2ℓ), where ℓ has original density ℓ/2; thus E(D⁻¹)=π/2. The fourth latitude is uniform on [−1,1]. Dividing its interval probability by ε gives pointwise 6/D with integrable universal bound 6/D, hence P(V≤ε)~3πε and a joint weak limit of the first triple tilted by 2/(πD), followed by circle-arclength uniform P4. Reweighting the first chord ℓ/2 by π/(2ℓ) and 2/π gives limiting constant chord density 1/2 on (0,2); permutation exchangeability gives all six edges. The argument explicitly handles measure-zero collinear triples and boundary |h|=1, and asserts weak not total-variation convergence for the unmarked points. Inspected the full RESULT proof and attached Monte Carlo checker path; the latter is empirical corroboration, not a proof.
